clue.text: A water heater might be low priority

definitions.meaning: a boiler set behind a kitchen range or fire, heating water
matters put aside to simmer for later are said to be on this

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the boiler could be left for another day.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear stove ring or boiler heats water, and the idiom for a postponed task names that same rear cooking position.

clue.text: Long for a church service's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for the close of a long church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn or pine for something is to long for it.

clue.text: Master mariner executed for getting fish

indicators.note: an executed person loses the head, so the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a ship's captain is its skipper

explanation.surface: A ship's captain is put to death for stealing fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoked herring is a common British breakfast fish.

clue.text: In front of the judge, drunk and tense

parts.note: to be up before the judge is to appear in court
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A defendant appears in court intoxicated and nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anxious and on edge is described as wound up or strained.

clue.text: A small cut obtained from prison?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a jail or police station

explanation.surface: A minor wound picked up while behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a shallow notch, and in British slang also a jail or police station.

clue.text: Give back the others before losing half

parts.note: the rest means the remaining ones

indicators.note: the six-letter word before drops its first three letters, half of it

explanation.surface: Return what remains, before giving up half of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To return something to its owner or former state is a synonym.

clue.text: Farm animal under trees a long time is a bird

indicators.note: in a down clue the animal sits beneath the trees

parts.note: a wood is a group of trees
a pig is a farm animal
an eon is an age, a very long time

explanation.surface: A pig lingers beneath the trees for ages — and it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large grey dove common in British woodland and farmland.

clue.text: The sort of light under which to display Chilean red?

indicators.note: to display letters here is to lay them out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A host asks what lamp would best show off a bottle of Chilean red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging, branched ceiling fitting holding many lights.

clue.text: Sap from lettuce hearts

parts.note: cos is a variety of lettuce
H is the card-playing abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Juice drawn from the inner leaves of a lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sap' looks like plant juice, but here it is a club; 'hearts' is not the lettuce's core but the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sap is a short weighted club or truncheon, the same weapon as this word.

clue.text: How to eat cuts of meat with signs of approval?

parts.note: chops are cuts of lamb or pork
ticks are marks showing something is right

explanation.surface: A question on dining manners about meat dishes awarded marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The paired sticks used for eating in East Asian cuisine are a method of eating.

clue.text: Lean and working, showing sinew

parts.note: to tend is to lean or incline towards
on means operating or working

explanation.surface: A slim, active person shows off their muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of tough tissue linking muscle to bone is a sinew.

clue.text: Where fires start raging in moorlands?

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the moorland word

parts.note: heaths are open moorlands

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Asks where wildfires begin on the open moors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fires' suggests wildfires, but the definition means domestic fireplaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireplace floor is where a household fire is laid.

clue.text: Person who's mostly compassionate to scrounge outside home

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: humane means kind and compassionate

indicators.note: the begging word goes around the home word

parts.note: to beg is to scrounge
in means at home

explanation.surface: A kindly soul who scrounges away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the species Homo sapiens is a person.

clue.text: Corrupt mature middlemen on charge

parts.note: adult means mature
the middle of the word men is E
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Grown-up brokers are accused of crookedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middlemen' reads as brokers, but splits as the middle of men, E; RATE is placed after it ('on').
explanation.definitionFit: To corrupt a substance is to debase it with impurities.

clue.text: Rock salmon starter — and then fish!

indicators.note: a starter is the first letter of the word

parts.note: hake is a fish

explanation.surface: A menu offers a salmon starter and then a fish main course.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock something is to jolt it back and forth.

clue.text: Quietly live to obtain control

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to reside is to live somewhere

explanation.surface: Advice to live discreetly in order to gain power.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting is to be in control of it.

clue.text: Rings friends to welcome sweetheart

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the friends word holds the heart letter

parts.note: pals are friends
the heart of the word sweet is E

explanation.surface: Someone phones friends to greet a beloved partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Peals are loud ringing sounds of bells.

clue.text: A crowd, perhaps, runs into you — once

indicators.note: the runs letter goes inside the old word for you

parts.note: thee is an archaic word for you
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A mob charges into someone, long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'two's company, three's a crowd', hence the 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says two make company and this number makes a crowd.

clue.text: A rough scramble in the noisy shopping centre

indicators.note: noisy says the shopping word is heard rather than written

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A rough scuffle breaks out in a loud shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, a loose struggle for the ball among standing players; generally a rough tussle.

clue.text: Trade licence covering store

indicators.note: the words trade licence cover the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A trading permit is required to run a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a food shop or store.

clue.text: Reported row to head

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the rowing word is heard

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat

explanation.surface: A dispute is reported to the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like an argument, but it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony case of the head is used to mean the head itself.

clue.text: Flexible, within the limits of secular slide

indicators.note: the supple word sits inside the outer letters
limits are a word's first and last letters

parts.note: lithe means supple, flexible

explanation.surface: Something supple slides within worldly bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To slither is to slide or glide along like a snake.

clue.text: Well-read and inclined to protect rebel leader

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the inclined word wraps the leader

parts.note: leaned means inclined or tilted

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A scholar who is minded to shield a rebel chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarly and educated, someone who has read widely.

clue.text: Distinguished, but lacking ability

definitions.meaning: read as two words, unable or incapable

explanation.surface: Eminent, yet hopelessly incompetent.
explanation.definitionFit: Means remarkable or eminent, and split in two says someone is incapable.

clue.text: Discussion group for preparing marines

indicators.note: preparing suggests the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A briefing meeting to get the marines ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A class meeting for discussion, typically at a university.

clue.text: One short story, one chapter of writing, perhaps

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single brief tale, one chapter of a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type is an example of a style of printing or handwriting.

clue.text: Wandering harangue on royal

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: ER stands for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina
to rant is to harangue

explanation.surface: A stray tirade aimed at a royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight errant roams in search of adventure: it means wandering or straying.

clue.text: Silly Billy going to earth

explanation.surface: A fool heading to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt is called this, and so is a lump of soil.

clue.text: Leave quickly and fasten the door

definitions.meaning: to secure it with a sliding bar

explanation.surface: Rush out and lock up behind you.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash off is to flee, and a sliding bar secures a door.

clue.text: Not a wholly admirable hold!

parts.note: read admirable as admiral-able: only part of England's most famous admiral, giving a wrestling grip

explanation.surface: A grip that is not entirely praiseworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is admirable/admiral: Horatio Nelson was Britain's great naval hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestling grip, arm under the opponent's armpit and hand on the neck, is named this.

clue.text: Putting the gun back means curtains

indicators.note: putting a word back reads it in reverse

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Returning the weapon spells the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtains' suggests death or the end; here it is net curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: Net curtains are a light window covering.

clue.text: Edited with care in order to perform a ceremony in church

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them anew

explanation.surface: Text revised carefully so a church service can be held.
explanation.definitionFit: To consecrate a building again is a churchly ritual.
